- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- Model frequently overpredicts mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day mean is > 68.0, cap forecast at 68.0–70.0 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to adjust forecast midpoint.
- If true outcome is > 10% above model forecast, check if sentiment was negative 3–5 days prior — if so, model may be underreacting; adjust up by 1–2% for next period.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3 days show downward momentum, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0% downward bias unless sentiment is strong bullish.
